invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.
Every changed page keeps working without JavaScript; JavaScript only enhances it (conflicts:c-006).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).
'Save and return to overview' saves without the page's required-answer checks, but still refuses an answer that fails its own format rule (conflicts:c-211; ruling:sam-2026-10-07).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.title: Commodity pages chain as journey steps around the main import reason
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 makes the two commodity pages steps of the journey rather than an overview task that returns to the overview. The commodity page's back link goes to origin and Save and continue goes on to the main import reason; Commodity details comes after the main import reason, its back link goes to the commodity page, and Save and continue goes on to identification, additional or arrival details, whichever applies first. The k6 performance suite's live-animals step list walks the new order in the same change, so the suite keeps running.

increments.title: The germinal commodity search offers V4's germinal products, and only them
increments.detail: The germinal set's 'What are you importing?' page is the finished live-animals page with a germinal hint and its own catalogue. Following V4's germinal data fields and the 9 October ruling, the catalogue holds V4's germinal commodities with embryos and ova as separate items, each offering the species Design Release 2.1 lists, and the live-animals catalogue gives up the 12 germinal lines it holds today, so neither set offers the other's commodities. Searching and ticking behave as the live-animal search does.
acceptanceCriteria: The germinal 'What are you importing?' page keeps the live-animals title, caption, heading, ITAHC inset, label, buttons, Cancel link and Back link to the origin page, and its search hint reads 'You can search for semen, ova or embryos, or by common name (for example, cattle), Latin name (Bos taurus) or commodity code (05119985).' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-057, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-058; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p1-097)

The germinal catalogue holds 18 items, sorted by name, codes shown with their leading zero: Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep each as '<Animal>, Embryos' and '<Animal>, Ova' (05119985); 'Cattle, Semen' (05111000); and 'Cat, Semen', 'Dog, Semen', 'Goat, Semen', 'Horse, Semen', 'Pig, Semen', 'Rabbit/Rodent, Semen' and 'Sheep, Semen' (05119985). There are no Cat or Dog embryos or ova and no poultry, fish or bee germinal products. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-050 to -p1-063; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-037, -p1-038; conflict c-230 default)

increments.title: Germinal Commodity details asks total gross weight, number of packages and temperature, and the backend stores them
increments.detail: The germinal set's copy of Commodity details asks, for each chosen species, an optional 'Total gross weight' in kilograms and a 'Number of packages', and always asks one optional 'Temperature' for the consignment. A germinal commodity has one Selected commodities row. The animals backend stores the gross weight as a decimal and the temperature on every line, and shows them back; neither is published, because the current PIMS profile (gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0) has no field for them. A germinal notification is published on the same GBN-AG events as a live-animals one, each trade line carrying the typeCode for its product type.
acceptanceCriteria: Each germinal species block asks 'Total gross weight' in a narrow text input with the suffix 'kg', before 'Number of packages'; left blank it shows no error. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-030; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-031; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-032; confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-011; conflict c-232)

Each germinal species block asks 'Number of packages', with no hint and no '(when required)', and never asks the number of animals. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-029, prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-034; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-032, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-034; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-033)

After all commodity blocks the page always asks one 'Temperature' radio question, its legend at label size rather than a heading, hint 'How will the products be stored', options Ambient, Chilled and Frozen in that order; left unanswered it shows no error. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-039, prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-040; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-033; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-034; confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-019 to -p1-025; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-021; conflict c-232)

A germinal commodity has one Selected commodities row listing all its chosen species, such as '05111000 | Cattle, Semen | Bos taurus'; its block is headed '<name> (<code>)', such as 'Cattle, Semen (05111000)', and its species sections are separated by section breaks. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-030; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-031)

A saved total gross weight such as 24.5, the number of packages and the temperature are shown again when Commodity details is reopened; the backend holds the weight as that species line's gross weight in kilograms, as a decimal, and the temperature on every commodity line of the notification. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-022, -p1-040, -p1-042; confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p1-006, -p1-012; repo:backend repo-backend-p1-039, repo-backend-p1-040, repo-backend-p1-043, repo-backend-p1-044; conflict c-022)

The GBN-AG notification the backend publishes for a germinal notification uses the same events and payload as a live-animals one: each trade line's quantity is its number of packages, it carries no gross weight and no temperature, and it leaves out unweaned animals, CPH number and permanent address as it leaves out any unanswered section. In that published payload each germinal trade line carries the typeCode SEMEN for a semen item, EMBRYO for an embryos item and OVA for an ova item, and embryos and ova are always separate trade lines. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-036 to -p1-038; repo:backend repo-backend-p6-109; conflict c-273)
In the published GBN-AG payload every live-animal trade line carries typeCode LIVE_ANIMAL (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-039; repo:backend repo-backend-p6-109, repo-backend-p6-039)

increments.title: Hard stops: means of transport on arrival details and number of packages on commodity details
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 makes the means of transport the only hard stop on 'Arrival details', because it decides whether transit countries apply; the other arrival answers can be left for later. On commodity details the number of packages becomes a hard stop, alongside the number of animals, on each line that asks for it.
acceptanceCriteria: On 'Arrival details', 'Save and continue' with no means of transport chosen is refused with an error on the means of transport question. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:162)

On 'Arrival details', 'Save and continue' with a means of transport chosen and the arrival date, port of entry, transport identification and transport document reference blank goes on to the next page. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:158)

On 'Commodity details', 'Save and continue' with a line that asks for a number of packages left without one is refused with an error on that line's number of packages. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:162)

On 'Commodity details', a line that does not ask for a number of packages can be saved without one. (prototype:dr2-1-specs COVERAGE.md:162; repo:frontend src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/lines.js:4-8)

increments.title: Main import reason completes on its own answers, and both pages soft-save as Design Release 2.1 does
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 judges the main import reason task on the reason's own answers, with Additional details its own task. 'Save and return to overview' saves what is valid and returns to the overview without the page's required-answer checks, so a trader can leave part-way through. An answer that breaks its own format rule, such as an impossible exit date, is still refused, because the service cannot store it.
acceptanceCriteria: With an allowed reason and its valid follow-ups saved (Internal market with a purpose; Transhipment or onward travel with a listed country; Transit with a listed port and country; Temporary admission horses with a real exit date and a listed port; Re-entry alone), the overview shows the main import reason task as complete while Additional details is still unanswered (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-080, prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-081)

increments.title: Arrival details requires a means of transport, and arrival and transit return to where the trader came from
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 makes means of transport the one required answer on arrival details, because it decides whether transit countries are asked. It also sends a trader back to where they started: the overview when they opened the page from the overview, the review when they came from the review. 'Save and return to overview' lets a trader leave a part-finished page without a means of transport. The real service keeps every field check it has today (c-045): a page with any error saves nothing and shows the entries back, and an answer that cannot be stored, such as an impossible date, is refused even on 'Save and return to overview' (c-211).
acceptanceCriteria: Save and continue on arrival details with no means of transport chosen stays on the page and shows 'Select a means of transport to the port of entry' in the error summary, linking to the means of transport select, and above the select, which is shown in its error style (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-039, prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-040; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p8-030, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p8-031)
When that error shows, the page title starts 'Error: ', nothing is saved and the other answers entered are shown back (conflict c-006; conflict c-045)

'Save and return to overview' on arrival details with an impossible arrival date, such as 31/2/2027, stays on the page with 'Enter a real arrival date' and saves nothing (conflict c-211; conflict c-045; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p11-019)

notes: Combines req-315 (means of transport required), req-327 (return to overview), req-328 (return to review) and req-329 (Save and return to overview): all four decide what Save and continue and Save and return do on the same two pages, and each criterion needs the others' set-up to observe.

c-045 keeps today's field checks, so the prototype's soft-validation claims are not built; c-211 keeps format checks on 'Save and return to overview'. The arrival date is typed as day/month/year, so the impossible-date example is written that way.

Depends on inc-002 (journey-foundation), which changes the live flow so a page opened from its overview task returns to the overview; Sam's 9 October ruling (claim 39) adds no marker to the address, so this row uses that mechanism rather than building a second one. increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 saves a complete document and moves the trader on at once when they press Save and continue, even while a document is still being scanned, and applies the same check before Save and return to overview, saving a document whose type is chosen. openQuestions: CDP must raise the nginx ingress request-body cap in front of trade-imports-animals-frontend to at least 50,001,024 bytes, and the service team must record the confirmation against EUDPA-518, before this is built and deployed. Until then the limit stays at 10MB everywhere.

One limit applies in every environment and every set: if the germinal-products documents page (req-1825) has been copied before this unblocks, this row raises its limit too, and its criteria then hold on both sets' documents pages.

increments.title: An empty species panel is refused on its own save, even beside a filled one
increments.detail: One identifier is enough to save a live animal (9 October ruling), but an animal with no identifier at all is not a record. Today 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal' fires only when nothing is typed anywhere on the page, so with two species an empty panel's save is skipped silently while the other's data is there. The check moves to each panel: a panel save with every identifier of its current animal blank is refused on that panel. The page's own 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' still never block on missing identifiers, and the page still shows no message about the submit rule.
acceptanceCriteria: With cattle and dogs on the page, an ear tag typed into the cattle panel and nothing typed into the dog panel, pressing the dog panel's 'Save and add another' saves nothing and shows 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal' in the 'There is a problem' summary and inline on the dog panel's first identifier field; the summary link focuses that field. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-027, repo-frontend-p6-118; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p5-019; conflicts:c-042)

Pressing 'Save and finish' on a species' last animal still to enter, with every identifier of that animal blank, is refused the same way and the animal stays to enter. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-027; conflicts:c-042)

The per-panel check refuses only a wholly blank animal: a cow given only an ear tag and saved with its panel button saves with no error, is listed in the saved-animals table with an empty Passport cell, and the panel moves on to the next animal. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-188; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-019; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p6-102)

'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' with every form on the page blank show no error, save no animal and move on. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-071; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-065; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-028; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p6-106)

increments.title: Identification counts as complete only when every animal is entered, and submit needs one entry per species when several are selected
increments.detail: Today the hub's Identification details row shows Complete straight after Commodity details, before any animal is identified, and stays Complete at 1 of 2. DR2.1 counts identification complete only when every animal of every selected species with identifier fields has a complete entry. For submitting, DR2.1 makes identification optional for a single species but needs at least one complete entry per species when more than one species is selected; the identification page itself shows no message for that rule.
acceptanceCriteria: Straight after Commodity details, with no animals entered, the hub's Identification details row does not show Complete. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-068; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p6-002; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p10-003-m1)

With 1 of 2 cattle entered, the row does not show Complete; once both are entered with ear tag and passport it shows Complete. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-068; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p6-066)
A selected species with identifier fields but no number of animals keeps the row from showing Complete. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-068)
With one species selected and no identification entered, the notification can be submitted. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-070)

With two species with identifier fields selected and one of them without any complete entry, submitting is refused; once each has at least one complete entry, submitting goes ahead. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-070; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p5-020)
The identification page shows no message about the submit rule. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-070)
notes: Combines the hub completion rule and the submit rule: both read the same 'complete entry' definition from the every-identifier row and change the same obligation evaluation. The submit refusal's place and wording belong to the review-and-submit area, which owns the submit gate and its messages (req-animal-identification-056's why); the criterion asserts only that submitting is refused or goes ahead. If that area drafts a row for the same gate, the combiner should merge this submit criterion into it or set dependsOn. The germinal half of the completion rule (a germinal species counts once its entry is saved) is proved in the germinal panel row. Builds after the every-identifier row in this area.

Dropped: req-248 and req-249 are adopted as already met. ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claims 13, 36 and 37 split off their germinal halves and settle that one identifier is enough for Complete and for submit, which the live-animals code does today; the germinal bar is req-261 in inc-183.

increments.title: A permanent address page for cats, dogs and ferrets, with one card per animal and a same-as-destination choice
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks for each pet's permanent address on its own page in the consignment parties section, opened from the consignment addresses page, instead of inside the animal identification form. The page has a card for each cat, dog or ferret (not other live mammals), showing the identifiers already given, and asks for each one whether the animal lives at the place of destination or at a new address, revealing the address fields only when a new address is chosen. Each animal's choice and address are stored with the notification, every field in its own place, and a trader can save what they know and come back.
acceptanceCriteria: A consignment with cats, dogs or ferrets has a 'Permanent address' section on the consignment addresses page explaining 'A permanent address is where an animal:' with the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address' to the permanent address page; for cats alone there is no CPH section (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-023, p9-025; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-085, p7-106; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-081)

A consignment of other live mammals alone has no permanent address section, and opening the permanent address page for it sends the trader to the consignment addresses page (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-023, p9-024; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-109; document:dr1-parity-backlog p6-012, p6-015)

The permanent address page has the caption 'Consignment parties', the heading 'Permanent address', the browser title 'Permanent address - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and a back link to the consignment addresses page (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-021, p9-032, p9-033; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-109, p13-110; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-082, p3-108)
The animal identification page no longer asks for any address field (document:dr1-parity-backlog p6-058; trace:e2e p6-028)

The page shows one card for each animal that needs a permanent address, as many as were entered for each species, headed with the scientific name and a running number such as 'Felis catus 1'; species that do not need one get no card (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-037, p9-038; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-091, p13-111; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-084)

Each card shows the animal's entered identifiers in inset text as 'label: value', such as 'Microchip: MICROCHIP-1', leaving out blank ones, and shows no inset when none are entered (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-039; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-111)

Each card asks 'Select an address' with the options 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' and 'Enter a new address', neither chosen when the page first opens; once a place of destination is given, the first option's hint is that address on one line, such as 'Riverside Holding Facility, East Farm Road, Leeds, LS25 3EB, United Kingdom' (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-040, p9-041, p9-042; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-092, p7-094, p7-095, p13-112; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-085)

An animal saved as 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' has the place of destination's name, address, country, email and phone as its permanent address on the review page, and reopening the permanent address page shows that option selected (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-067, p9-068; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-115; prototype:dr2-1-specs p4-039)

increments.title: The permanent address page checks each new address and names the animal in every error
increments.detail: With several animals on one page, the trader must be told which animal each error is about. A new address's name, first line, town, postcode, email and phone are required exactly when 'Enter a new address' is chosen, and the same-as-destination choice cannot be used before a place of destination exists. What the trader chose and typed is kept through an error and when the page is reopened, and the page explains what to do when no animals have been counted yet.
acceptanceCriteria: With 'Enter a new address' chosen and the fields left blank, saving shows 'Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address' and 'Enter a phone number' on those fields; address line 2 and county are optional, and email, phone and postcode are checked only for being blank (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-054 to p9-061; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-101; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-105; trace:e2e p6-036 to p6-042)

Each address error in the error summary names its animal, such as 'Enter address line 1 for Felis catus 1', and links to the field; the message on the field itself leaves the animal out (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-054 to p9-059; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-100; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-091)

Choosing 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' before a place of destination is given shows 'Add a place of destination before you can continue' on that animal's radios and in an error summary titled 'There is a problem', linked to the radios (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-053, p9-053-m1; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-096; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-088)

When the page shows errors, every animal's chosen option stays selected and a chosen 'Enter a new address' stays open with what was typed; reopening the page later shows each animal's saved choice selected and its saved address filled in (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-064, p9-064-m1; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-100-m1; trace:e2e p6-043)

increments.title: The permanent address leaves the identification page
increments.detail: Today cat and dog panels carry a fraud warning, a permanent-address definition, the question 'Where will their permanent address be?' and eight address fields under the identifiers, validate them all-or-nothing, store the address on each animal and show it as a 'Permanent address' column. DR2.1 asks each animal's permanent address on its own permanent address page in consignment parties, so it leaves this page with its validation, its table column and its storage from here. The 2026-10-07 ruling is the fresh ruling DR1's address block waited for (c-044).
acceptanceCriteria: Cat and dog panels no longer show 'Providing a false address is an act of fraud', the permanent-address definition, the question 'Where will their permanent address be?' or any of its eight address fields. (ruling:sam-2026-10-07 ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-008; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-029; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p6-028)

increments.title: The address book record carries the address's type and what it can be used for
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks what type of address is being added and what it can be used for, and Sam's 9 October ruling keeps both answers because a question the service asks must persist and DR1 asked for address pickers filtered by role (c-176). Today the address-book record is untyped and its API carries no type or use, so nothing can keep those answers, and the address book list's type tabs and the DR1 role-filtered pickers have nothing to filter on. Afterwards an API caller can create, read and update an address with its type and uses, in a field shape the address-book service designs in its own conventions, and addresses saved before the change still read back.
acceptanceCriteria: Creating an address through the address book API with its address type and one or more uses (place of origin, consignor, place of destination, consignee, importer, branch address) stores them, and reading the address back by id returns the same type and the same uses (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-079; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-081; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-137; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-115, p1-116)
Updating an address through the API with a different set of uses replaces its uses with the new set, and the read-back shows the new set (repo:addressbook p2-071; prototype:dr2-1-source p16-079)

A create or update carrying a use outside those six is refused with a 400 validation problem whose errors name the uses, and nothing is saved (repo:addressbook p1-039, p1-045; ruling:sam-2026-10-07 p1-010)
An address created without a type or uses, and every address saved before this change, is still accepted and reads back with no type and no uses (repo:addressbook p1-001, p1-003)

The address book's locked API contract describes the type and uses on the create and update requests and on the read response, with the six allowed uses (repo:addressbook p2-097, p2-098; document:dr1-parity-backlog p7-064, p7-065)
increments.gate: Check the type and uses field names, the six use values and how a record without them reads back in the locked contract, before the add form, the address book list's type tabs and the DR1 address pickers build on it.
notes: Pass 1 slice on its own: the typed record is the foundation the add form's uses question, the list's type tabs (address-book-list area) and DR1 inc-047/inc-048 rest on, so it lands first and gates. Observable through the API in every environment the tests repo's address book API client reaches (local stack and CDP). Rewritten for Sam's 9 October ruling: the record now carries the address's type as well as its uses (req-1256), the field names and shape are the address-book service's (c-176; ruling claims 66, 70, 116), so no criterion names the prototype's 'primary type' or 'address book type'. The old criterion that a stray 'type' or 'role' field is still refused is dropped: c-176 leaves that rejection for the service to keep or replace when it names its new fields. Type and uses stay optional on the API so a journey's handshake add and every existing record keep saving; the add form makes a use required outside a journey. Updates fully replace the editable fields today, so the edit page must post the stored type and uses back; that is the edit row's criterion. Decision: refuse an unknown use with a 400, because the record only means something with known values (validation clause of ruling:sam-2026-10-07).

increments.title: Address validation messages match Design Release 2.1, on the form and in the API
increments.detail: Four required-field messages change wording to match Design Release 2.1 and their field labels. The address book API's messages change with them, because the API's message reaches the user when the service rejects a save. Afterwards the add and edit forms, and the API's validation problem, give the new wording.
acceptanceCriteria: Saving the add or edit form without a name shows 'Enter a name or organisation name' inline and in the 'There is a problem' summary, and the address book API's blank-name validation message is 'Enter a name or organisation name' (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-071, p16-066; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-070, p16-114; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-129, p6-162; repo:addressbook p1-010)

Saving without a postcode shows 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', and the API's blank-postcode message is the same (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-074, p16-069; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-073; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-132; repo:addressbook p1-021)

Saving without a country, or with a country not in the list, shows 'Select a country', and the API's blank-country message is the same (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-075, p16-070; repo:insfrontend p3-055, p3-056; repo:addressbook p1-025, p2-023)

Saving without a phone number shows 'Enter a phone number', and the API's blank-phone message is the same (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-077, p16-072; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-075; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-134; repo:addressbook p1-028)
notes: Unchanged by the 9 October ruling. Pass 1 had one slice per message; pass 2 combines them because each makes the same two edits (the form's copy and the API's message) on the same review and ladder. Kept apart from the record row because it carries no structural change and can land in parallel. The other required-field messages already match (exists). Today's length limits and email format check stay (req-1244, exists; c-179, which the germinal data fields' Standard Address Block confirms); whether phone gains a telephone-format check is a question (req-1869, c-256), not built here. Welsh drafts for the new strings are the Welsh row's.

increments.title: Adding an address starts by choosing its type
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks what kind of address is being added before any fields, because the type decides the form and the uses offered next. Today the address book's add is the address form itself. Afterwards 'Add a new address' on the address book opens a new 'Choose an address type' page, on a path of its own in the INS front door's path shape; choosing Origin or Consignor, Destination, Consignee or Importer, or Branch moves on to the address form, which stays where it is today (the page the animals frontend's handshake links to), retitled 'Add address and contact details' and able to go back to the type page. The chosen type is remembered while the add is in progress and cleared when it starts afresh or saves. Transporter is its own row.
acceptanceCriteria: From the address book list, 'Add a new address' opens a page with the caption 'Add a new address', the heading 'Choose an address type', a radio group whose legend repeats the heading visually hidden, and a 'Back' link to the address book list (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-001, p16-003, p16-004, p16-005, p16-013; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-038, p16-039; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-104, p6-105, p6-106, p6-112)

The options are, in order: 'Origin or Consignor' (hint 'Place of origin, Consignor'), 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' (hint 'Place of destination, Consignee, Importer'), 'Transporter' (hint 'Private, Commercial') and 'Branch' (hint 'Branch address'), with a 'Continue' button (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-006 to p16-010, p16-012; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-040 to p16-043; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-107 to p6-111, p6-113)

Continuing with no type chosen shows 'Select an address type' inline on the radios and in a 'There is a problem' summary whose link goes to the first option (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-016; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-045; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-114, p6-115)

Choosing 'Origin or Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' or 'Branch' and continuing opens the address form, which posts back to itself and shows the caption 'Add new address', the heading 'Add address and contact details', no notification status banner, and a 'Back' link to 'Choose an address type' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-018, p16-019, p16-021, p16-022, p16-023, p16-024; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-047, p16-053, p16-069; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-116, p6-117, p6-118; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-090)
Opening the address form outside a notification journey with no address type chosen goes to 'Choose an address type' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-020)

Going back from the address form to 'Choose an address type' shows the chosen type selected; opening 'Add a new address' again from the address book starts with no type selected and empty fields, and after a save the next add starts empty (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-002, p16-011, p16-087)

The browser titles read 'Choose an address type - Import notification service - GOV.UK', 'Add address and contact details - Import notification service - GOV.UK', and on the edit page 'Edit address and contact details - Import notification service - GOV.UK', keeping the 'Error: ' prefix when a page shows errors (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-038, p16-053, p16-107; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-104, p6-117, p6-158; trace:ins-fit p1-003, p3-003)

The address types offered when adding an address read, in this order and with these hints: 'Place of Origin' ('The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain'), 'Consignor' ('This is the sender of the consignment.'), 'Consignee' ('This is the receiver or buyer of the consignment being shipped or transported.'), 'Importer' ('This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed.'), 'Place of Destination' ('This is where the animals will be unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours. If a health certificate is required, it will show this address.'), 'Transporter' ('This is the person or company responsible for transporting the consignment.'), then, after a divider, 'Branch Address' ('This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.') (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-105, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-111; repo:tests repo-tests-p5-095)
increments.gate: Check the two-step add and its in-progress state, which the add-details, manual-entry and transporter rows copy, and that a notification journey's handshake into the address form still opens it directly, without 'Choose an address type', and returns the new address id (c-106).
notes: Rewritten for Sam's 9 October ruling (claims 72, 73, 75, 90): the address form stays at the address book's existing add path (the one the animals frontend's handshake links to) and the type step takes a new path in the INS front door's path shape, rather than moving the form to the prototype's /add/lookup; no criterion names a path. The previous open question on the handshake (journey mode) is settled by c-106: keep today's handshake, and in journey mode the form skips the type step; that behaviour is req-1284's row. Pass 1 slices combined: the type page, its error, its options, the hop to the address form and the form's caption, heading and back link all share one route pair and one review. The address form reuses today's fields at first; its content changes in the next rows. Title format: the suffix comes from the shared INS layout, which the address book list and the layout area also change; make the change once there. The k6 performance suite's add scenario posts to the address form with no type; a save without a type keeps working until inc-070 makes the save need a type and a use, so the suite's change (req-1870) is in inc-070 and there is no perftests change here. Welsh drafts are the Welsh row's.
The combiner adds req-1859, which no area drafted: it is the type step's options and hints.

increments.title: The add-details form for an address entered by hand
increments.detail: The address form's address and contact fields take Design Release 2.1's layout and copy: 'Address' and 'Contact details' section headings (also on the edit form), the 'Name or organisation' label, no County field, new widths, an alphabetical country list with United Kingdom pre-selected for Origin or Consignor and a 'Select one' placeholder, and cancel as a link under the button. Today the add form has 'Enter address details' and 'Enter contact details' headings, a County field, United Kingdom always first and a secondary cancel button.
acceptanceCriteria: On the add-details step and the edit page the address fields sit under the section heading 'Address' and Email address and Phone number under 'Contact details' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-038, p16-049, p15-062, p15-063; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-055, p16-062, p16-108; trace:ins-fit p1-008, p1-018, p3-005-m1)

On the add-details step the name field is labelled 'Name or organisation', while the edit page keeps 'Name or organisation name' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-039; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-056; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-121, p6-161-m1)
The add-details step has no County field (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-045; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-054)

On the add-details step 'Name or organisation', both address lines and 'Email address' are full width, 'Town or city' and 'Postcode or Zip code' half width, and 'Phone number' two-thirds width (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-059, p16-060, p16-064-m1)

On the add and edit forms the Country select lists reference data's countries in alphabetical order, with United Kingdom in its alphabetical place (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-065; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-110; c-177)
For 'Origin or Consignor' the Country select opens with United Kingdom selected, and its blank first option reads 'Select one' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-047-m1; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-078)

Below 'Save and continue' the add-details step has a 'Cancel and return to address book' link, not a button, that goes to the address book and saves nothing (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-065; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-068, p16-134)
notes: Depends on 'Adding an address starts by choosing its type' (the add-details step it changes). Pass 1 slices combined: section headings, label, County, widths, country order and default, placeholder and cancel are all copy and layout on the same form and review together. The section headings and the alphabetical country order are asserted on both forms because each requirement says 'add and edit'; the edit page's own order, widths and placeholder are the edit row's. What the country list holds is reference data's unfiltered list, MDM's content (c-177, req-1235 exists); nothing here waits on MDM. In journey mode the cancel stays the journey's own (req-1284's row), so this row's cancel link is the address book add's.

increments.title: Address book list: Design Release 2.1 intro, filter disclosure, search control, table cells, empty state and a banner that stays
increments.detail: The INS address book list changes to Design Release 2.1's layout and copy. The intro is reworded and set in large body text, 'Add a new address' moves directly under it, and search moves into a collapsed 'Filter addresses' disclosure with a plain 'Search' label, a placeholder instead of a hint and an icon-only search button. The 'Clear search' link goes. The table shows a multi-word name on two lines and every stored address line on its own line. An empty book or a search with no match shows the same table with 'Showing 0 of 0' instead of a message, and the success banner no longer hides itself after 3 seconds. All of this is the same list page and template, so it is one review.
acceptanceCriteria: Under the 'Address book' heading the list shows, in large body text, 'Manage your addresses for use across all your import notifications' in place of 'Manage addresses used across import and export services.' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/address-book.html:35-41; trace:prototype-dr2-1 list-categories-pagination-and-filters action 20; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/address-book.fit.spec.js:27)
The 'Add a new address' button comes directly under the intro, above the 'Filter addresses' disclosure. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/address-book.html:44-48,54-58)

The search field sits inside a collapsible 'Filter addresses' disclosure with a chevron, built on the GOV.UK details component and collapsed when the list loads, so the search field is hidden until the user opens it. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/address-book.html:54-58; trace:prototype-dr2-1 list-categories-pagination-and-filters actions 69-70; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/address-book.fit.spec.js:29,59-61)

The search field is labelled 'Search', in place of 'Search addresses'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/address-book.html:64-76; trace:prototype-dr2-1 list-categories-pagination-and-filters actions 71-72; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/address-book.fit.spec.js:62)

The search field shows the placeholder 'Search by name, address or country' and has no hint. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/address-book.html:64-76; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/address-book.fit.spec.js:63)

The search field has an icon-only search button whose accessible name is 'Search', and no visible 'Search' text button; with JavaScript off, pressing Enter in the search field submits the search. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 list-categories-pagination-and-filters actions 71-72)
No 'Clear search' link shows, whether a search found addresses or found none. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/address-book.html:50-139)

In the Name column a name of more than one word shows on two lines, the first word then the rest, such as 'Green' then 'valley farm'; a one-word name shows on one line. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/data/address-book.js:103-111; trace:prototype-dr2-1 list-categories-pagination-and-filters action 20)

After an add, edit or delete the success banner is still showing 10 seconds after the list loads; it no longer hides itself. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/address-book.html:24-31, app/routes.js:10014-10026)
notes: Combines three thin slices on the same list page and template: the heading area and search control (req-1112, 1114, 1115, 1116, 1117, 1118, 1133), the table cells (req-1136, 1137) and the empty state and banner (req-1132, 1147). Built apart they would repeat the same list template, copy file, fit spec and E2E page object for little gain. c-171 settled that the empty and no-match messages, the Clear search link and the timed banner go. The Type select joins the 'Filter addresses' disclosure in the Type-filter row; until then the disclosure holds the search field alone. Live filtering as the user types belongs to the search row (req-1121); here the search still submits as a GET form. Each new English string gets a Welsh machine draft as it is added; req-1186's completeness check is the Welsh row. The success-banner client script is removed or stops hiding the banner; the client entry file is shared.

increments.title: View an address: GOV.UK page titles, optional rows only when filled, a secondary Edit button and no 404 for a dead link
increments.detail: The address book pages take Design Release 2.1's page titles, with the GOV.UK suffix and a hyphen separator. The k6 suite (req-1870) is changed here, on this row's branch name, as c-225 settles: this is the row whose save first needs a type and a use and returns to the list filtered by type, which breaks the suite's direct post to the add form; the type step the suite now chooses on lands in inc-061, which this row follows.

increments.title: Destination, Consignee or Importer and Branch addresses entered by hand, with a fixed UK country

acceptanceCriteria: For 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' the add-details step opens with the address fields, contact fields and uses question shown and no address search, in the fit suites, on the local stack and in every CDP environment (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-178, p1-182; prototype:dr2-1-source p16-036; c-217)

increments.title: The address search finds UK addresses as you type, once the address lookup is real
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 opens Destination, Consignee or Importer and Branch addresses on a free-text type-ahead search that fills the address from a picked result, with manual entry as the way round it. Its results must be real UK addresses from the address lookup the INS backend serves (c-178). Sam's 9 October ruling blocks all of it until the address lookup becomes a real feature of the INS front door and INS backend: today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page. When it lands this area is re-distilled and this row rewritten to what search then needs, including which environments it runs in.
acceptanceCriteria: For 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' the add-details step opens with only the address search; the address fields, contact fields and uses question stay hidden until an address is picked or manual entry is chosen, and open already revealed when an address or address line 1 is already present (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-025, p16-037; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-083, p16-096, p16-098; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-140, p6-141)

Typing in the address search lists matching addresses below it in a list labelled 'Address search results', each shown as the lookup's formatted address line with the typed text in bold, and a screen-reader announcement gives the number of results, such as '1 result available' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-027, p16-029, p16-030; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-086, p16-086-m1; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-143; c-178)

Picking a result hides the search, announces the selection to screen readers and reveals the fields filled from it: premises to address line 1, street and locality to address line 2, town to town or city, the postcode, and country United Kingdom; name, email address and phone number stay blank, and anything the user types over a filled field is what is saved (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-033, p16-034, p16-035; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-087, p16-088, p16-089; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-145; repo:insfrontend p5-052 to p5-059; c-178)

Saving the search layout with nothing picked or typed shows the six field errors with the address and contact fields revealed, so each error summary link moves to a visible field; the errors stay until the next save, and the typed values, ticked uses and search text are kept (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-077; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-092, p16-094; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-142; repo:insfrontend p3-065; c-180)

Once it lands, re-distil this area: which environments the search runs in, what else it needs, and these criteria per environment are settled then.
notes: Rewritten for Sam's 9 October ruling: the search row and the search parts of the previous 'Destination, Consignee or Importer and Branch' row (req-1214, req-1285) stay in the backlog, blocked on the lookup, so the manual-entry row can build now. The earlier default (stub locally, real lookup in CDP dev, off elsewhere) is replaced by the ruling, so the per-environment criteria are gone until the re-distil. The lookup returns no organisation name, so the screen-reader announcement names the picked address (c-178). The spike page itself stays as it is (out of scope). The Welsh for the search's strings is this row's own, since the Welsh sweep row no longer waits for it.

increments.title: Editing an address matches Design Release 2.1
increments.detail: The edit page takes Design Release 2.1's heading, field order, layout and country select, returns the user to where they came from on Back and Cancel, keeps the address's type and every use it has, words its success banner as Design Release 2.1 does, and sends the user back rather than to an error page for an address not in their book. Today the heading is 'Edit address details', Phone comes before Email, the fields use other widths, the country select keeps a placeholder, Back and Cancel ignore any return path, and unknown ids show page not found.

notes: Depends on 'The address book record carries the address's type and what it can be used for' (the kept type and uses: an update fully replaces the editable fields, so the edit must post the stored type and uses back) and on 'The add-details form for an address entered by hand' (the section headings and country order it shares). Sam's 9 October ruling: the return parameter's name is the service's and its allow-list stays (claim 92), so the criteria say where Back and Cancel go, not how the return is carried. A valid edit still returns to the list's default view (exists). The reconciler settled req-1277 without the prototype's blank-name fallback ('Address updated'): the edit form and the address book API both require a name, so no valid edit has a blank one, and the fallback is not built. The edit page's Cache-Control is left as it is (out of scope). Pass 1 slices combined: every criterion is on the one edit page and its save.

increments.title: Destination-side journey add pages find UK addresses by search
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1's consignee, importer and place of destination add pages, reached from the journey through the INS frontend's address book (c-106), start with a UK address search, as the address book's own 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' step does. Every searching add-address page offers the same search, lists matching UK addresses from the INS backend's address lookup (c-178), fills the form from a pick, offers manual entry and keeps the fields hidden until needed. Sam's 9 October ruling blocks all of it in every environment until the address lookup becomes a real feature; until then the pages open on manual entry (built in inc-078), and the area is re-distilled once the lookup lands (c-217).
acceptanceCriteria: The consignee, importer and place of destination add pages and the address book's 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' add-details step start with a text field labelled 'Search for an address', placeholder 'Start typing...', browser autocomplete turned off, and a search icon button whose accessible name is 'Search' (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-086; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-042, p7-043; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-069)

Typing lists matching UK addresses from the address lookup under 'Address search results', each a button showing the lookup's one-line address with the typed text in bold, and no Northern Ireland address (postcode starting 'BT') is offered (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-086, p8-087; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-046, p7-053, p7-063; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-073; conflicts:c-178)
Screen readers hear the result count through a polite live region, such as '3 results available' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-047)

Picking a result hides the search, reveals the form and fills address line 1, address line 2, town or city and postcode with country United Kingdom, all editable, leaving the name, email address and phone number empty for the trader, because the lookup gives no organisation name; earlier error messages stay until the next submit (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-089; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-048 to p7-050, p7-048-m1, p7-052; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-074; conflicts:c-178)
Picking a result whose lookup address has a locality keeps the locality in the filled form, in address line 2 with the street (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-048-m2; conflicts:c-178)
An 'Enter address manually' link-styled button below the search reveals the address and contact fields without a search (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-088; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-045)

On the journey add pages the address fields and the 'What else should this address be used for?' checkboxes stay hidden until a result is picked or manual entry is chosen, and show again after a failed submit when anything was entered or picked (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-091; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-042-m1; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-070)

Submitting a journey add page before picking or entering anything shows, in order, 'Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address', 'Enter a phone number', with no country error and no search error, and reveals the fields so each error summary link reaches a visible field (prototype:dr2-1-source p8-099; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-051; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-071; conflicts:c-109)
openQuestions: Blocked (req-647 to req-654 blockedBy, c-217): the INS backend's address lookup must become a real feature. Today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page and not wired in. Who: the team building the INS address lookup. Once it lands this area is re-distilled, which settles which environments the search runs in and what else it needs (ruling 2026-10-09 p1-178, p1-180).
notes: Was todo, now blocked: Sam's 9 October ruling (c-217) replaces the earlier per-environment default (stub locally, real lookup in CDP dev, off elsewhere) with no search in any environment until the lookup is real, so the per-environment criteria and the default question are gone. Manual entry is not blocked: the destination-side pages open on manual entry in inc-078. dependsOn moves from inc-077 to inc-078, which builds that manual-entry page this row adds the search to. One slice: the search, its results, the pick, the manual fallback and the hidden-until-needed form are one behaviour, built on the address book's search row (inc-072), also blocked. The address book's own search field (req-1215) and manual entry (req-1219) were folded into req-647 and req-652.

increments.title: The journey add page's Country select offers the countries reference-data serves from MDM
increments.detail: On the place of origin and consignor add pages the trader picks the address's country by hand. Sam's 9 October ruling takes the MDM block off this row (c-107): the select offers reference-data's unfiltered country list, which is what MDM serves, and no list is typed or edited in code. Where MDM's content differs from Design Release 2.1's 42 entries, such as the EU outermost regions and the Crown Dependencies, that is MDM's content to change. The stub tidy-up regenerates the local country fixture from MDM, so the names and counts the page's checks expect move to the recaptured fixture. Observable in the INS frontend's fit suite, on the compose stack and in CDP.
acceptanceCriteria: On the place of origin and consignor add pages the Country select offers every country in reference-data's unfiltered /countries response for that environment, with the names it serves, and no country it does not serve (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-129, p1-132, p1-143; conflicts:c-107)

On the compose stack the select holds as many countries, with the same names, as the stub's regenerated MDM country fixture serves unfiltered, not today's 32 sovereign states (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-150, p1-155, p1-162; trace:e2e p9-064)

The end-to-end and fit checks of the select take their country names and counts from the captured reference-data fixture, and no country list is typed by hand in them (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-144, p1-159, p1-160)
notes: Was blocked on the MDM integration; ruling 2026-10-09 (p1-129 to p1-133, through c-107) unblocks it, so it is todo. The 42-entry Design Release 2.1 list is not built: the claims behind it are overruled by c-107 and no longer cited. Ruling p1-149 makes this row depend on the stub tidy-up row at the head of the reference-lists theme (inc-173), because it changes the names and counts these checks assert. The stub tidy-up row owns regenerating the stub and capture fixtures (trade-imports-stub, the INS frontend's 4 hand-typed stub countries, ins-tests' country-codes); this row only aligns the add page and its checks. Today the INS select pins United Kingdom first and drops GB from the list; that ordering is not list content and is kept.

increments.title: Welsh for the redesigned address book list, view and delete pages

increments.title: The CPH number page follows Design Release 2.1: who is asked, its help and hint, a blank save, and where it goes
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks for a county parish holding (CPH) number for every live animal kept on a holding, not only today's short list: in the live-animals set every commodity but horses (0101) and the pet code 01061900 (cats, dogs, ferrets and other live mammals) gets the question, and the page cannot be opened for a consignment it does not apply to. The page's help gains a second place to find the number, the hint loses its punctuation, the boxes stop browsers offering saved values and bring up the digit keypad, and a trader can save the page blank and move on, with the gap held at submission instead. The page is a step of the consignment addresses section: it is opened from that page and always returns to it. Every changed English string gets its Welsh machine draft in the same change.
acceptanceCriteria: A live-animals consignment holding cattle, ornamental fish, pigs, sheep, goats, chickens, turkeys, ducks, geese, guinea fowl, rabbits, camels, ostriches, parrots, reptiles or bees is asked for a CPH number; one holding only horses, cats, dogs, ferrets or other live mammals is not, and its consignment addresses page has no CPH section (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-001, p9-002; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-106; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-110; trace:e2e p6-068, p6-070; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-025, p1-057)

The CPH help's second paragraph reads 'You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK.', with 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' a link to https://www.gov.uk/guidance/get-a-county-parish-holding-cph-number (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-009; trace:animals-fit p13-018; trace:e2e p6-084)

increments.title: The germinal set's own review: germinal answers in their species blocks, its unfinished-species messages, and no CPH or permanent address
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 reads a germinal product's total gross weight, package count, temperature and identification details back on the review. The 9 October ruling builds germinal products as their own set, each page a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the prototype's germinal differences, and keeps this row's germinal content for the germinal set's copy of the review. The germinal set always asks for temperature, takes weight as a decimal total gross weight in kilograms, and stores and shows its germinal details even where PIMS does not carry them.
acceptanceCriteria: In the germinal-products set's review, each species block shows 'Total gross weight' as '<n> kg', a decimal weight such as '12.5 kg' reading back as entered, and 'Number of packages' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-083; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-022)

increments.title: Addresses card: permanent addresses, CPH format, one header link and a single unfinished entry
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 shows pets' permanent addresses in full in the Addresses card, writes the CPH with slashes, gives the Addresses and Contact address cards one header Change link and no row actions (c-138), returns a CPH change made from the review to the review (c-141, settling DR1 parity row inc-146's open question), and lists one error summary entry per unfinished card, so a deleted saved address is named once, on its card (c-135).
acceptanceCriteria: In the live-animals set, pets' permanent addresses read back in the Addresses card as a 'Permanent address' subsection, one entry per animal labelled '<common name> <n>' (for example 'Domestic cat 1') with the full address and 'United Kingdom', without email or phone, and the identification table has no Permanent address column (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-111; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-152, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-153)
The CPH number reads back with its parts separated by slashes, for example '12/345/6789' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-160, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-154)

No party row and no contact address row carries an 'Edit details' link: the Addresses and Contact address cards' header Change links are their only links (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-067; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-151; c-138)

Moving the permanent address out of the identification table touches that table too; the identification row owns the table's other columns. The CPH page's own return behaviour may need the change context the CPH page reads (cph-permanent-and-contact area's page). The tests repo's page object clicks 'Edit details' today and follows the header link. req-848 is the live-animals set's only: the germinal set's review has no Permanent address subsection and no CPH row (req-1843, germinal-products area).

increments.title: The review page reads each party's copied address back as name, address lines and country
increments.detail: The trader checks the address copy the notification holds before submitting. Design Release 2.1 reads each consignment party and the contact address back as the name followed by the address lines and the country, each on its own line, with no telephone number or email address. Today the review shows each copy as a block with the name in bold and every non-empty field, telephone and email included. Observable in the animals frontend's fit suite, on the compose stack and in CDP.
acceptanceCriteria: On the review page each consignment party with an address reads back as its name, then each non-empty address line, town or city and postcode, then the country, each on its own line (prototype:dr2-1-source p11-065, p11-114; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p12-160, p12-161, p13-151, p13-155)
A country of GB reads back as 'United Kingdom' (prototype:dr2-1-source p11-114; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-155)

The review page and its party rows are the review-and-submit area's code: combiner, merge this row with that area's review-card row if one changes the same 'Roles and addresses' or contact cards. The end-to-end specs that read every copied field back from the review page (copied addresses, submit freeze, address edit) will need their review assertions updated to the new read-back.

increments.title: Review ends with Continue and Delete, and an amendment's review offers Cancel amend and tells the trader they are re-submitting
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 ends an editable review with Continue and a red Delete. While amending, it adds a 'Cancel amend' button, retitles the review 'Review before re-submitting' once something has changed, and opens with no errors shown. The ruling's validation override still refuses an incomplete resubmission and says why (c-136). What the delete and cancel-amend confirmations do is the manage-notifications area's.
acceptanceCriteria: An editable journey or draft review ends with 'Continue' and, beside it, a red 'Delete' button that opens the notification's delete confirmation (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-115, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-118; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-162, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-157; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-084)

While a notification is being amended, the review ends with 'Continue', which submits, a secondary 'Cancel amend' button that opens the cancel-amendment confirmation, and a red 'Delete' button that opens the delete confirmation; there is no 'Cancel amendment' link (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-117; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-068, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-086)

An amendment's review is headed and titled 'Review your notification' when first opened, and 'Review before re-submitting' once any notification answer differs from the submitted version (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-019, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-082, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-083; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-064, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-065)

Changing only the uploaded documents during an amendment leaves the heading 'Review your notification', because only notification answers count as a change (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-084)
An amendment's review opens with no error summary and no card errors, even when answers are missing (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-040, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-041; c-136)
Pressing Continue on an amendment that is not complete does not submit it: the review is shown again with its error summary naming what is missing (c-136; ruling:sam-2026-10-07)
notes: Pass 2 combines the review's end actions with the amendment review's heading and error behaviour: all are the review's own controls and state, with the same amend set-up. The backend already keeps a pre-amend snapshot of the notification separately from its documents; telling the frontend whether the notification answers differ from it is the backend part of this slice. The tests repo asserts today that a draft review has no Delete, and the cancel-amend spec uses the 'Cancel amendment' link; both follow. Delete and cancel-amend confirmations belong to manage-notifications; this row only links to them.

increments.title: A submitted notification's view has a header: reference, status, date submitted and a Back link to the overall dashboard
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 heads a submitted notification's view with its reference and status, dates it, and sends the trader back to the overall dashboard, which is the INS front door's (c-143, c-198). The 9 October ruling keys the header on the real route and the stored status, and keeps dashboard draft rows going to the hub. This row builds the header for Submitted, Submitted action required and Completed; the draft's own header at the same review route (c-246) is the row after the header actions, because it reuses them. The page title keeps the page name before the service, as accessibility requires (c-006). Opening the view of a notification that does not exist goes to the overall dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: A submitted notification's view shows its notification reference as the h1 in place of 'Review your notification', with its status beside it as a tag reading 'Submitted' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-021; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-179, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-173; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-067, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-090; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-096)

A submitted notification's view has the page title '<reference> - Import notification service - GOV.UK', while the journey review of a draft or an amendment keeps 'Review your notification - Import notification service - GOV.UK' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-173; c-006)

Under the header, a submitted notification's view shows 'Date submitted: <d Month yyyy>', the date it was submitted (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-024; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-092; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-174)

On the workspace stack and in CDP, a submitted notification's view has a Back link to the overall dashboard in the INS front door (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-005, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-016; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-101; c-143; c-198; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-120)
Opening the view of a notification that does not exist goes to the overall dashboard (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-002, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-007; c-198)
increments.gate: Look at how the page tells a submitted notification's view from the journey review (keyed on the route and stored status), and at the view header: the header-actions, action-required and completed rows all build on this header.
notes: Re-drafted for the 9 October ruling (claims 96 and 97): the header is keyed on the real route and the stored status, not on 'opened from the dashboard'. c-246 settles that a draft's review, at the same route, also shows the header with the Draft status and stays editable (req-900); that is inc-187, which follows the header-actions row because the draft's header carries Copy as new, Delete and the Import reference numbers too. Pass 2 combines the view header (reference, status, title, date submitted) with its navigation (Back link, missing notification): one page state, one set-up. The backend already stores the submitted date but the view data carries only the created date; returning the submitted date is the backend part. The Back link and the missing-notification redirect use the animals frontend's configured INS front-door URL, which has a default; req-899's fallback to the set's own root when no INS URL is configured must be kept, but it is not written as a criterion because the setting always has a value in every environment this row runs in. Status tags for 'Submitted action required' and 'Submission complete'/'Completed' are the action-required and completed rows'. 'Copy as new', 'Delete' and 'Amend this notification' in the header are the header-actions row's.

increments.title: View header offers Amend, Copy as new and Delete, and shows the import reference numbers to copy

Each state-changing control looks as Design Release 2.1 draws it but submits a form with the CSRF token (c-189). What amend, copy and delete do is the manage-notifications area's.

The Submitted action required and Completed states' buttons are checked in their own rows.

increments.title: Submitting records its date and outstanding items, and a notification still missing its health certificate shows as 'Submitted action required'
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 records the submission date and what is still outstanding at the declaration, and shows a notification submitted without its health certificate as 'Submitted action required': read-only, with a warning saying what to do, the missing certificate marked in section 4, and a Continue that leads back to the hub. The real service can only change a submitted notification through an amendment, so that Continue starts one (c-144). The identifier-driven items are a separate row.
acceptanceCriteria: After declaring and submitting, the notification's view shows 'Date submitted: <the day it was submitted>', and the same date on every later visit (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-145, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-155)

On an action-required notification with no uploaded document, '4. Uploaded documents' shows the error 'Upload a valid health certificate' in place of document cards, inline, with no error summary (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-107; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-099)

The action-required view ends with 'Continue', which starts an amendment of the notification and opens its hub, where the trader can upload the certificate (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-120; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-041; c-144)

The action-required view header offers 'Amend this notification', 'Copy as new' and 'Delete' as a Submitted notification's does (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-025, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-027, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-029)
notes: Depends on the rows 'A submitted notification's view has a header…' and 'View header offers Amend, Copy as new and Delete…'. Pass 2 combines recording the submission (date and outstanding items, req-909) with the action-required view it feeds: the view's status, warning and date come from the stored record, so neither is observable alone. How action-required is stored is the real team's design (9 October ruling, claim 98): the criteria name only what the trader sees. A re-submission from an amendment works the items out afresh. increments.title: Declaration page: small checkbox in a hidden-legend fieldset, and no status strip

increments.title: A completed notification shows as complete with no Amend button
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 shows a finished notification as 'Submission complete' (or its own status text, such as 'Completed') and stops amendment. No completed status reaches the real service today: post-submission outcomes come from the authorities' case system, which sends none back yet.
acceptanceCriteria: A completed notification's view shows the status tag 'Submission complete', or its own status text such as 'Completed' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-022; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-103; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-099)
