openQuestions: A real source of completion must exist before the completed tag can show: no completed status reaches the service today, and the 9 October ruling (claim 99) names no provider. The likely one is the authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sending post-submission outcomes back to the notification record (as req-1082). Until somebody names and builds that source, nothing here can be built or seen.
notes: Blocked: req-910 carries blockedBy on a real source of completion (9 October ruling, claim 99). Once unblocked, it lands after the rows 'A submitted notification's view has a header…' and 'View header offers Amend, Copy as new and Delete…', and alongside whatever row builds that source.

increments.title: Tests prove the review, declaration and confirmation paths no test covers today
increments.detail: Today's suites leave several review, declaration and confirmation paths unproven, and many of them change in this programme. After this row each one has a test that fails if the behaviour breaks.
acceptanceCriteria: A test proves the review of a notification with several commodity lines reads back each commodity card and each species block with its rows (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p13-133; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p25-087)

A test proves the review's party address errors: a copied address that breaks the address-book rules and a deleted saved address each show their messages and links (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p13-134; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p13-071)

A test proves how the review shows a rejected document and a document still being scanned (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p13-134; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p25-088; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p13-067)

A test proves Cancel amend on the amendment review and each view header button (Amend this notification, Copy as new, Delete) leads where it should (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p13-133; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p13-101, trace-e2e-p13-105)

A test proves the confirmation page for a notification submitted with an ITAHC uploaded shows no outstanding documents item (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p14-063; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p26-057)

A test proves the declaration's refusal path: a ticked declaration on a notification the review refuses is not submitted and the trader is told why (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p14-064; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p26-059)

A test proves a failed submit and a stale submit (a notification changed or already submitted elsewhere) leave the notification unsubmitted and tell the trader (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p14-064; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p26-060)

A test proves a declaration ticked on an incomplete notification is refused and the trader is sent back to the review naming what is missing (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p14-064; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p14-021; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-087)
notes: Depends on every todo row in this area whose behaviour it proves (commodity cards, Addresses card, documents cards, amendment review, view header actions, confirmation page), so each test asserts the Design Release 2.1 behaviour rather than today's. Each criterion is proved at whichever level fits (frontend fit spec or the tests repo's end-to-end suite); the planner picks. A failed or stale submit is driven through the backend's real refusal, mocked only at the network boundary in fit tests. The view header buttons are proved on a submitted notification, following c-246's default.

increments.title: Overview totals count only positive numbers
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1's Overview adds only positive counts to the Animals and Packages/boxes totals, so a card never shows a negative or odd total. Held until the reconciler says how such a count could reach the Overview.
acceptanceCriteria: On the Overview, the Animals and Packages/boxes totals add only the positive counts on each commodity line: a zero, negative or non-numeric count adds nothing, and a total that is not above zero reads '0' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-014, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-015; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p4-010)
openQuestions: Sent back to the reconciler: no trader can enter a zero, negative or non-numeric count (the commodity details page refuses any number of animals or packages below 1, and a template is seeded from the same checked answers), so the change cannot be observed in any environment. The reconciler decides whether req-787 is already met as far as anyone can observe, or names how such a count can reach the Overview.
notes: Drafted by the combiner: the notification-hub drafter listed req-787 as unobservable. It is held here, blocked on the reconciler's answer, so the buildable Overview rows are not held up.

Dropped: the reconciler adopted req-787 as already met (delta exists). Commodity details refuses a number of animals or packages below 1 or not whole, and templates are seeded from the same checked answers, so no zero, negative or non-numeric count can reach the Overview; blank counts already add nothing and both totals already read 0 before any line exists.

increments.title: Fallback warning for an action-required notification's other outstanding items
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 shows a general warning on an action-required notification whose outstanding items are about neither identifiers nor documents. Held until the reconciler names an outstanding item that can trigger it.
acceptanceCriteria: An action-required notification whose outstanding items are about neither identifiers nor documents shows the header warning 'You need to complete missing information before import' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-030, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-034)
openQuestions: Sent back to the reconciler: the real service has no outstanding item other than the ITAHC/documents item and the identifier item (itself blocked on DR1 inc-103, c-133), so no notification can reach this state and the warning cannot be observed in any environment. The reconciler names an outstanding item that triggers it, or puts req-904 out of scope until one exists.
notes: Drafted by the combiner: the review-and-submit drafter listed req-904 as unobservable. It is held here, blocked on the reconciler's answer.

Dropped: the reconciler put req-904 out of scope. The only outstanding items the real service records are the ITAHC or documents item and, once DR1 inc-103 is ruled, the identifiers item, each with its own warning, so the fallback warning has nothing to trigger it. It comes back into scope with any new kind of outstanding item.

increments.title: Amend this notification asks for confirmation in a dialog, then opens the amend review
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks a trader to confirm before amending a submitted notification, in a dialog over the view page, and then takes them straight to the notification's review page so they can see and change their answers. Today the amend action has no confirmation and lands on the overview hub, one step away from the review. After this change 'Amend this notification' opens a modal dialog ('Amend notification', 'Are you sure you want to change this notification?') whose 'Yes, continue' starts the amendment and lands on the amend review, the dashboard card's Amend lands on the same review, and an amend that cannot happen returns the trader to the overall dashboard. Because a state change must stay a form post carrying the CSRF token (c-189, kept by the 9 October ruling), the dialog's confirm submits a form, and without script the same control reaches a confirmation page with the dialog's heading, question and buttons (c-190). The k6 performance suite's amendment check moves with the landing in the same change (c-225).
acceptanceCriteria: On a Submitted notification's view page, 'Amend this notification' opens, without leaving the page, a dialog with the level-1 heading 'Amend notification' and the question 'Are you sure you want to change this notification?' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-046, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-047; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-181, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-175, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-056, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-057; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-108)

The dialog's 'Yes, continue' button starts the amendment and the trader lands on that notification's review page, showing it is being amended, not on its overview hub (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-048, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-081; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-058, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-062; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-110, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-124; c-191)

The dialog's link-styled 'No, go back' button closes the dialog, leaving the notification Submitted and the trader on the view page, from where 'Amend this notification' opens the dialog again (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-049; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-059; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-109-m1)

The dialog is hidden until opened; once open it is announced as a modal dialog named by its heading and described by its question, with a Close (X) button announced as 'Close' and an overlay behind it; the Close button, the overlay and 'No, go back' each dismiss it without amending (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p1-029, prototype-dr2-1-source-p1-030, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-050, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-054, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-055; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-183, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-060, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-061, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-084)

Amend for a notification that is not Submitted (such as one already being amended from another tab) or whose reference is unknown changes nothing and returns the trader, with no message, to the overall dashboard: on the workspace stack and in CDP the INS front door's dashboard; in the animals frontend's own fit run, which has no INS front-door URL configured, /live-animals (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-091; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-129; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-075; repo:backend repo-backend-p2-092, repo-backend-p2-093; c-198)

notes: Pass 2 combines the dialog (req-1391, req-1392, req-1393), the landing on the amend review (req-1394), the amend guard (req-1487) and the k6 amendment journey (req-1877): one route, one dialog, one review and ladder. req-1393 covers both dialogs; this row builds the shared dialog, and the cancel-amendment row shows it holds there too. Today 'Cancel amendment' navigates to a separate page with the journey strip, a Back link, an explanatory paragraph and a 'No, return to notification' button, and the restored view shows a Success banner. After this change the cancel confirmation opens as a dialog over the page, keeps a no-script confirmation page at today's route (c-190), lands on the plain read-only Submitted view with no banner, and a cancel for a notification not being amended returns to the overall dashboard. The 9 October ruling keeps ?cancelled=1 on the redirect (c-268): the address stays, the banner goes.

increments.title: Copy as new carries over exactly Design Release 2.1's list, from the submitted version
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 says what a copy keeps (origin, internal reference, what is imported with its species, the reasons and their follow-ups, the additional animal details, the parties and CPH) and what it leaves for the trader to fill in again (numbers of animals and packages, identifiers, arrival, transit, transporter, documents and contact address). Today the backend copy mapper and the pages disagree: the record clears the internal reference, the species, the unweaned answer and the exit date, yet the copy's overview shows counts, identification, arrival, transit, transport and contact address as Complete because the whole answer payload is copied. c-196 settles that a copy carries exactly Design Release 2.1's list, in the record and on the pages alike, and c-197 that copying an amendment in progress copies its submitted version. After this change a copy keeps and clears what Design Release 2.1 says, and a certified-for value no longer offered is mapped to a current one.
acceptanceCriteria: A copy's origin of the import comes back with the source's internal reference number, and the copy's review shows it (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-063; c-196)

increments.detail: Copy as new is checked against the version of the notification the trader was looking at, so a copy of something that has changed since is refused with 'The notification has been updated'. After this change a stale copy returns the trader to where they started, the dashboard or the notification's view page, with the banner, and copies nothing. The 9 October ruling keeps this row because it fixes a real bug.

increments.title: After a delete the trader lands on the overall dashboard, which says 'Notification has been deleted'; an amending notification can be deleted
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 sends the trader to the overall dashboard after a delete. Today the trader lands on the live-animals dashboard at /live-animals?deleted=1 with the banner 'The notification has been deleted.' (req-1707 records today's shared copy). The 9 October ruling drops the session flash and keeps ?deleted=1 on the redirect, and c-269 settles that the page the delete lands on shows the message, in Design Release 2.1's wording for when the reference is not known: 'Notification has been deleted'. Deleting a notification being amended already works, but nothing proves it and the backend's API description still says only drafts and submitted notifications can be deleted. After this change the delete lands per c-198 with ?deleted=1, the landing page shows the new message, the API description lists AMEND, and the end-to-end suite proves deleting an amending notification and the guard redirects of amend, cancel amendment, copy and delete, still asserting ?cancelled=1 and ?deleted=1 and keeping its smoke-tagged cancel and delete cases.

increments.title: The live animals list moves to the INS frontend, scoped to the trader's organisation
increments.detail: Following Rhys's DR1 judgement that the animals dashboard is temporary and moves to the INS front door (c-159, kept by the 2026-10-09 ruling for that judgement alone), the INS frontend serves the live animals notification list, in its own path shape, from the INS backend read model, and the live-animals set root in the animals frontend stops rendering a list and sends the trader there. The page takes Design Release 2.1's frame: the 'Dashboard' title and caption, the 'Live animals' heading, a Back link to the overall home, a 'Create new' link that starts a live animals notification in place of today's draft-creating start form, a 'Use template' button, the 'Notifications' heading and cards named for screen readers. Persistence and authentication are real constraints, so the list shows only the signed-in trader's organisation's notifications and the list API refuses a caller that names no organisation. The k6 journey script, which reads the list from the set root today, follows the move (ruling p1-199). Every new string ships with a Welsh machine draft. This row sets the page, the cross-service hop and the scoping every later list row builds on.
acceptanceCriteria: A signed-in trader opening the INS frontend's live animals list sees the browser title 'Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK', the caption 'Dashboard' and the h1 'Live animals'. The INS front door lists those notifications at /actions, across every category or only the one it is showing, scoped to the signed-in organisation. manage-notifications' inc-126 still says the delete lands on the overall dashboard with no 'deleted' marker; the 2026-10-09 ruling p1-101 keeps ?deleted=1, so the combiner should reconcile this row's landing with that area's rewrite of inc-126.

The page lists, under a visually hidden h2 'Notifications chosen for inspection', every one of the organisation's notifications chosen for inspection across all categories, including ones whose status has moved on such as Completed, with no category filter (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:6753-6755, 9094, 7442; trace:prototype-dr2-1 inspection-required snapshot 14)

The page has the same 'Search by' form and hint, 'Sort by:' select and 'Show <first>-<last> of <total> results' line as the Action needed page, pages 8 at a time, and its page links keep only the sort (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/dashboard-inspection.html:52-95; app/routes.js:6757-6807, 9108)

The page shows no 'Create new' or 'Use template' button and no glance cards; the 'Dashboard' navigation item is marked current on it; it shows the recoverable error with HTTP status 500 when the read model cannot be loaded, shows its copy in Welsh with Welsh selected, and has no serious or critical axe violations (trace:prototype-dr2-1 action-needed snapshot 14; repo:insfrontend src/server/app/features/dashboard/controller.js:113-126)

The germinal Status updates card waits with the blocked Status updated row, as the live-animals one does (c-148).

increments.title: Identifier-driven outstanding items: warnings, inline error, confirmation bullet and dashboard message
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 treats incomplete animal identifiers as an outstanding item: it names them in the action-required warnings, marks the species inline, adds a confirmation bullet and shows 'Information is missing' on the dashboard. The 9 October ruling closes DR1 inc-103 (one identifier is enough to identify an animal record) and removes this row's blocker (c-133). Identifiers are incomplete when a commodity line whose species asks for identifiers holds fewer identified animal records than the animals it declares, which includes a single-species consignment with no identifier saved.
acceptanceCriteria: A notification that meets the submission minimum, but has a commodity line whose species asks for identifiers holding fewer identified animal records than the animals it declares, is submitted with the outstanding item 'complete the animal identifier information in the notification', shown on the confirmation page (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-147; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-188, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-193; c-133)
A single-species consignment submitted with no identifier saved gets the same outstanding item on the confirmation page (c-133; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-147)

An animal record with one identifier filled counts as identified, so a notification whose every declared animal has a record with one identifier filled gets no identifier outstanding item (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-188, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-191)

An action-required notification missing both animal identifiers and its ITAHC shows the header warning 'You need to complete animal identifiers and upload a health certificate' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-031, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-034)

An action-required notification missing only animal identifiers shows the header warning 'You need to complete animal identifiers' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-032, prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-034)

On an action-required notification, a species that needs identifiers but has none shows 'Identification details' with the inline error 'Enter a minimum of 1 identifier' in place of its content, inline with no error summary (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-090; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-099; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-042 to trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-045)
On the dashboard, a submitted notification with its ITAHC but incomplete identifiers shows the error 'Information is missing' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-149; c-149)
notes: Unblocked by the 9 October ruling (claims 188 to 193): one identifier is enough, DR1 inc-103 is closed and not built, and inc-147's blocker is removed, so every requirement here is buildable now. Depends on 'Submitting records its date and outstanding items…' (inc-113), whose record of outstanding items this extends; on 'Action required on the dashboard…' (inc-131), whose read-model field carries the dashboard message; and on the identification details row (inc-106), the species block the inline error replaces. The same identified-record count decides submit and the hub's Complete status (claim 189); this row adds no stricter bar. The multi-line rule of inc-100 is written into the Behaviour Spec by that row (claim 194).

increments.title: Ask 'What are you importing?' before a notification is created
increments.detail: Starting a new notification from the all-types dashboard in the INS front door asks the Design Release 2.1 notification type question first, before any draft exists. Live animals carries on to the animals frontend's existing live-animals start, which creates the GBN-AG draft and lands on origin. Germinal products, offered second under the 9 October ruling, carries on to the start of the germinal products set, the live-animals set's sibling in the animals frontend mounted at /germinal-products; the ruling lets this link land before the set itself is built. Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products carry on to the start of the high-risk plants journey in trade-imports-plants-frontend. Abandoning the question leaves no empty draft behind.
acceptanceCriteria: Starting a new notification from the all-types dashboard shows the question 'What are you importing?' instead of going straight to an origin page, and no draft notification is created at that point: the dashboard's notification list gains no new entry while the question is open or after the user leaves it with Back (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11112-11114; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1; trace:e2e T01 call@286; conflicts:c-007)

The notification type page has the browser title 'What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and the heading 'What are you importing?' as the radios' fieldset legend (h1), with the caption 'About the consignment' inside the heading (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/notification-type.html:7,39; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16)

The question offers radios in this order, with no hint text on the group or any option and none pre-selected: Live animals; Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos); Plants for planting; Potatoes (seed and ware); Wood products (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:125-131; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 10; conflicts:c-007)

Choosing Live animals and pressing Continue creates a new live-animals draft and lands on its 'Origin of the import' page, which shows the Draft tag and a new GBN-AG reference (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:65; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 44; conflicts:c-007)

Choosing Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos) and pressing Continue sends the user from the INS front door to the germinal products set's start under /germinal-products in the animals frontend, and no live-animals notification is created: the dashboard's notification list gains no live-animals entry (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claims 1, 10 and 11; conflicts:c-007)

Choosing Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) or Wood products and pressing Continue lands on the start of the high-risk plants journey in the plants service, and no live-animals notification is created (conflicts:c-007)

Pressing Continue with nothing chosen re-shows the page with an error summary titled 'There is a problem' listing 'Select what you are importing', linked to the first radio, the same message shown inline on the radio group, and the browser title prefixed 'Error: ' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:151-160; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 30; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:53-57; conflicts:c-006)

The page ends with a single 'Continue' button: there is no 'Save and return to overview' button and no cancel link (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/notification-type.html:48-53; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16)
The page's Back link goes to the all-types dashboard, and the service navigation highlights Dashboard (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:10606-10608; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 15)

The page shows no Draft strip and no notification reference; the origin page reached after choosing Live animals shows both (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/notification-type.html:23-57; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16 against action 44; conflicts:c-007)

With Welsh chosen, every string on the notification type page (title, caption, heading, the five options, the error message and the Continue button) shows its Welsh counterpart (repo:frontend features/origin/copy/copy.cy.js:1-3)
increments.gate: Look at the cross-service start before anything builds on it: the type page in the INS front door, how Live animals hands over to the animals frontend's start (today a form post with its own request forgery token), how Germinal products hands over to the germinal set's start under /germinal-products before that set exists, and how the plants types hand over to the plants service. The re-selection row, template creation's type question, the INS germinal list's Create new and the dashboard's 'Create new' button all copy this pattern.
notes: Rewrites inc-148 to the 9 October ruling: Germinal products is now the second option (ruling claim 10 sets aside the old criterion 3 that left it off) and continues to the germinal products set's start, which the ruling (claim 11) lets land before the germinal theme builds the set. The criterion observes the handover to /germinal-products, never the germinal origin page, so it holds before the set exists; the germinal set's own create row proves the landing.

req-013 (the live-animals origin Back link) moves out of this row into the re-selection row (inc-150): its template-review branch can only be observed once template editing exists, and keeping it here would hold the whole start behind the templates rows. The ruling (claim 13) split req-013 into a live half (req-013) and a germinal half (req-1740, germinal theme).

Per conflicts:c-006 the page keeps the 'Error: ' title prefix in its error state. The all-types dashboard's 'Create new' button itself (c-147) is the dashboard-home area's change; this row repoints whatever start control the dashboard has at the time to the type question. The Welsh criterion carries req-057's duty for the strings this row adds; req-057 itself sits in the origin row that finishes the page.

increments.title: Origin's Back link follows where the notification started, and the type question picks the notification back up
increments.detail: The live-animals origin page's Back link follows where the user came from: the type question for a notification started from it, the live animals notifications list for one started there, the overview when opened from the overview, and the template review while a live-animals template is being edited. Going back to the type question shows the notification's own type already chosen. Keeping that type returns to the same notification with no new draft. Choosing a different type starts a new notification of that type in its own set or service, and nothing is changed or cleared on the notification left behind (9 October ruling, c-219).

increments.title: Manage templates page, empty, read from the user's stored templates
increments.detail: No real service has notification templates today. Design Release 2.1 adds a Manage templates page that lists a trader's saved templates. Templates are stored by the animals backend and kept between sessions, with no seeded examples (c-183). With nothing saved yet the page shows a zero count and an empty list. The page's path follows the real service's conventions, not the prototype's (c-258). Later rows add creating, viewing, using, changing and deleting templates on top of this page and store.

The page is named by page, never by the prototype's path (c-258, ruling claim 103). req-1310 (templates stored by the animals backend, no seeded templates) moves here from the save row: the empty, unseeded list is where it is first seen, and the store is built here; its kept-between-sessions half is observed again in the save row once a template can exist. req-1295 (Templates marked current) stays with the navigation row (inc-152).

Combines the page chrome (req-1291, req-1292, req-1294, req-1296), the list heading, count and empty state (req-1297, req-1298, req-1300), the GOV.UK component rule (req-1306), which every later templates page also follows, and the store (req-1310): one page, one set-up.

After a section is changed and saved, the template page's 'Date created' shows the day of that save (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-040; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T5 action 26)

A template never shows or holds an arrival date or time: answering one on the arrival page while creating it, or while changing its arrival details section, leaves the template page with no arrival date or time (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-043, p14-043-m1; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T3 action 20)
Leaving a change part way and opening the template page again abandons it: the template keeps its saved answers (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-054)
The change of a template that has been deleted goes to Manage templates (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-021; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:84-85)
notes: Re-distil (9 October ruling): the section allow-list criterion is withdrawn (req-1357 out of scope, c-263); the banner no longer dismisses itself (c-006); 'Template has been updated' for an unnamed template and the every-section criterion added (req-1361); req-1345 moved here from the view row.

Combines the change journey (req-1356, req-1358 to req-1361), the template page banner and abandon rule (req-1354) and the date-created reset (req-1343), all seen only by changing a saved section, plus the arrival-date rule (req-1345), whose second half needs a change. Eleven criteria because each section's change is reviewed once; split by section only if the plan finds it too big.
The 'Save and return' and 'Cancel' actions change the shared save-actions chrome every question page uses, and take precedence over the amend ending (req-1358).

increments.title: Use a template to start a notification
increments.detail: 'Use template' creates and saves a new draft notification in the template's own set, seeded from the template's answers, and opens its normal notification task list with a new GBN-AG reference. The arrival date is left to answer, no documents are carried, and the new notification starts with no validation errors. Other drafts are left untouched (c-183).
acceptanceCriteria: 'Use template', from a live animals template's card or its template page, creates a new live animals draft notification and opens its task list headed 'Notification tasklist' with the status 'Draft' and a new GBN-AG notification reference made the same way as any new notification's; the new draft is listed on the dashboard and the user's other drafts are unchanged (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T4 actions 7-14; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:54-59; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claims 27, 51; c-183)

The new notification uses the set's normal task list, including '4. Documents' and '5. Consignment parties', ending with 'Review and submit' and 'Return to dashboard', and nothing on it names the template it came from (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T4 action 14)
Its overview shows the template's animal and package totals under 'Your commodities' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T4 action 14)

It is seeded with the template's country of origin, region of origin ('Yes' with the code when the template has one, 'No' when not) and internal reference (blank when none) (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-062, p14-063)

It is seeded with the template's commodities and species, the commodity selections, animal and package numbers per species, net weight, package type and animal identification details (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-064 to p14-066; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 51)
It is seeded with the main reason for import, and with the purpose in the internal market only when the reason is 'Internal market' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-067)

It is seeded with 'Certified for' when the template's value is a valid option, otherwise 'Further keeping'; and with the unweaned animals answer when valid for the species, 'No' when the species have unweaned options and the template has none (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-068, p14-070; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 57)

It is seeded with the CPH number, port of entry, means of transport, transport identification and transport document reference, and leaves the arrival date empty, so Arrival details and Upload documents show 'To do' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-072; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T4 action 14)
It is seeded with the transporter's name, address, country, approval number and type (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-042; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T3 action 20; c-187)
It carries no documents and shows no validation errors when first opened (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-075)
Using a template that has been deleted goes to Manage templates and creates no notification (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-021)
notes: Re-distil (9 October ruling): the 'notification records the template's id and title' criterion is withdrawn (req-1366 out of scope, c-260); the notification starts in the template's own set (claim 51, c-266); req-1369 is now the live-animals half only (claim 57), so the storage-temperature seeding criterion leaves this row for the germinal half; the transporter-country question is settled (c-187), so the row carries no open question.

Combines every seeding rule (req-1363 to req-1365, req-1367 to req-1372): one action, one new notification, one set-up per check. Eleven criteria because the seeding rules are reviewed one by one; split only if the plan finds it too big.

Germinal: using a germinal products template, which starts a germinal products notification in the germinal set, is observed in req-1876's row once the germinal set exists; every criterion here is observed with a live animals template. Seeding party and contact addresses is in the card-answers row. Creating a seeded draft resembles copy-as-new: the plan may reuse the notification copy path.

increments.title: Template card answers, category and each party's address
increments.detail: Each template card lists Commodity, Origin, Consignee and Consignor and is labelled with the set the template was made in. A template saves each consignment party's address and the contact address as answered, shows them on its page, and seeds each back into a notification started from it, because the real notification persists and sends each party separately (c-186).
acceptanceCriteria: Each template card lists, in this order, Commodity (the commodity common names), Origin (the country of origin), Consignee (the consignee's name) and Consignor (the consignor's name), each reading 'Not applicable' when the template has no answer; a template saved with nothing answered shows 'Not applicable' for all four (prototype:dr2-1-source dashboard-template-card.html:15-34; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T9 action 78, T10 action 16; c-186)

A template made as a live animals template is labelled 'Live animals' on its card (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-014; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 24; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 51; c-266)

A template saves the place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and contact address each as answered, and its page's Addresses card (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination) and Contact address card show each of them as the design renders them (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T3 action 20; c-186)
Where the contact address was not chosen, the template's Contact address card shows the place of origin, as the design does (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-045; c-186)
A notification started from a template has each party and the contact address seeded as the template holds them (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-071, p14-074; c-186)

sources.ref: T1 action 24; T3 action 20; T9 action 78; T10 action 16

notes: Re-distil (9 October ruling): the category is the set the template was made in, not worked out from its goods (c-266); the party-address question is settled (c-186, kept by claim 125), so the row carries no open question.

Combines the card's answer rows (req-1304), the category label (req-1305) and party addresses (req-1346): the card's Consignee and Consignor come from the same saved party addresses. Depends on the save, view and use rows, since its criteria are seen on all three.

Germinal: the 'Germinal products' half of req-1305 is observed in req-1876's row (a germinal template is saved and listed with that category) once the germinal set exists; here the label is observed for a live animals template, so the row needs no dependency on the germinal theme.

increments.title: Sort by select on Manage templates
increments.detail: Manage templates has a 'Sort by:' select built as Design Release 2.1 has it: four options, the current one preselected, outside any form and with no apply button. As in the prototype it does not reorder the list (c-185), so 'Arrival date' needs no meaning for templates.
acceptanceCriteria: Manage templates has a 'Sort by:' select with the options 'Select one', 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', with 'Select one' preselected when no sort has been chosen (prototype:dr2-1-source dashboard-templates.html:63-74; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 24; c-185)
The select sits outside any form and has no apply button (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-009; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p15-016-m1; c-185)
With two templates saved, choosing any option leaves the list in its newest-saved-first order (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-009; c-185)
notes: Re-distil: c-185 now settles the sort question against the earlier default: the select is built as designed and does not reorder, so the row no longer needs the backend or the dashboard's sort pattern (dependency on inc-136 removed) and carries no open question. The select's name is the service's (c-258).
Kept apart rather than merged into the Manage templates row because its third criterion needs two saved templates (inc-157).

increments.title: Edit a whole saved template on its own task list
increments.detail: A saved template can be reopened at its edit address on its own template task list. Saving it from the review overwrites the template, keeping its address, and moves it to the top of the list.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening a saved template's edit address opens the template's task list ('Template tasklist', 'Template' tag and name) with the template's answers filled in (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8551-8569; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:88-90)

Saving the edited template from its review overwrites it: the list count is unchanged, the template keeps its address, shows the changed answer, and is listed first (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:7751, 7808-7818)
The edit address of a template that does not exist goes to Manage templates (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:8556-8560)
notes: Combines opening the edit (req-templates-072) and saving over the template (-051): an edit is only seen whole once saved. Depends on the save row.The template page has no Edit link (req-templates-061): the address is reached directly, so tests open it by address. The review's Delete button for a saved template being edited is in the delete row.

Dropped: ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 82 put req-1362 and req-1341 out of scope (c-261). Requirements kept as they were; the row covers nothing. The criteria are left as the row had them, for the record; the combiner may keep the row's earlier text unchanged.

increments.title: Discard a template being created
increments.detail: A template being created can be thrown away from its review, through the same 'Delete this template?' confirmation, without being saved. The confirmation uses the journey layout. The discard page shows only while a template is being created.
acceptanceCriteria: On the review of a template being created, the red warning 'Delete' button opens a page with the H1 'Delete this template?', a one-row summary list keyed 'Name' holding the name entered ('this template' when none), 'Confirm that you want to delete this template.' and 'This action cannot be undone.' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T11 actions 14-21; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:185-195; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 103)
The discard confirmation's Back link and 'No, cancel' link go to the template review (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T11 actions 19-21; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:193-195)
The discard confirmation uses the journey layout, not the dashboard layout (prototype:dr2-1-source delete-template.html:1,23)

Confirming 'Yes, delete' throws the template away unsaved and returns to Manage templates, list and count unchanged, with the success banner '<template name> has been deleted' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T11 actions 25-28; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:197-199)
Discarding a template with no name entered shows the banner 'Template has been deleted' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-087; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p7-185)

Opening the discard page when no template is being created goes to Manage templates, and confirming it then changes nothing and returns to Manage templates (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T12 actions 7-8; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:202-204)
notes: Re-distil: pages named by page (c-258, claim 103); the unnamed-template banner split into its own criterion so the reviewer checks the copy.

Combines the discard page (req-1380), its guard (req-1381), the outcome (req-1382) and the journey layout rule (req-1378, which the delete row's confirmation also keeps; observed for that page in inc-165). The prototype's unguarded discard post is not reproduced (req-1386 out of scope). req-1381 is kept: it is look and feel the trader can reach by Back, unlike the template URL guards claim 105 drops.

increments.title: Template review ends with Save template and Delete, and a saved template can be deleted
increments.detail: The template review ends with Save template and a Delete that discards a template being created or deletes a saved one, and a saved template can be deleted from its own page with Design Release 2.1's confirmation and banner.
acceptanceCriteria: The template review ends with 'Save template' and a red warning 'Delete' button that goes to the discard confirmation for a template not yet saved, which discards it, or to the template's delete confirmation for a saved template being edited, which deletes it (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-119, prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-084; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p15-093; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-067; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-103)

The template page's 'Delete' button opens a page titled 'Delete this template? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' with the H1 'Delete this template?', using the journey layout (prototype:dr2-1-source delete-template.html:1,6,23; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T8 actions 8-11; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:102-107; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 103)

The confirmation shows a one-row summary list keyed 'Name' holding the template's title (prototype:dr2-1-source delete-confirmation.html:6-8; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T8 action 12; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:109)

Under the summary it says 'Confirm that you want to delete this template.' and 'This action cannot be undone.' (prototype:dr2-1-source delete-confirmation.html:9-11; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T8 actions 13-14; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:110-111)

It has a red warning 'Yes, delete' button and a 'No, cancel' link back to the template page, in a GOV.UK button group (prototype:dr2-1-source delete-confirmation.html:13-21; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T8 actions 15-18; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:112)
Its Back link goes to the template page (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-080; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T8 action 16; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:107)

Confirming 'Yes, delete' removes the template and returns to Manage templates with one template fewer in the count and the success banner '<title> has been deleted' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T8 actions 22-29; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/templates.fit.spec.js:114-117)
After deletion the template's page, and its delete confirmation, go to Manage templates (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p14-021; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p7-184)
notes: Sits in inc-165 ('Delete a saved template') with the templates area's discard and delete requirements, which the combiner keeps there: the review's Delete is the way into those confirmations. req-943 is reworded by the 9 October ruling (claim 103) to name the confirmations by page, not by /templates/... path.

Re-distil (9 October ruling): the dependency on the dropped whole-template edit row (inc-163) is removed, and with it the criterion that the review's Delete goes to the delete confirmation for a saved template being edited: a saved template is never on a review any more (c-261). Pages named by page (c-258).

Combines the delete confirmation (req-1373 to req-1377), the outcome and banner (req-1379, req-1309). Depends on the view row (the Delete button) and the discard row (the shared confirmation page). Deleted templates are removed from the store, so the prototype's seeded-template resurrection does not arise (c-183).
Combiner: the review-and-submit area's req-943 (the review's Delete button) sat here before; with the edit mode dropped it is only the discard half, so consider moving it to inc-164.
The combiner merges the drafts of review-and-submit#15 and templates#13 into this row: they cover the same page and set-up, so building them apart would repeat the same review and ladder.

increments.title: Commodity pages return to where the trader came from: check answers, the overview or a template
increments.detail: A trader who opens the commodity pages from check answers, the overview or a template's review should come back there, not walk on through the journey. After a change from check answers, a valid Save and continue on both the commodity page and Commodity details returns to check answers, carried by the real service's change context; from the overview it returns to the overview; while editing a template from its review it returns to the template; and while creating a template a valid Save and continue on the commodity page goes to the overview.
acceptanceCriteria: After choosing Change on a commodity answer from check answers, a valid Save and continue on the commodity page and on Commodity details returns to check answers. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-100; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p5-038; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-103)
Opened from the overview, a valid Save and continue on Commodity details returns to the overview. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-100)

While editing a template from its review, a valid Save and continue on the commodity page and on Commodity details returns to the template's review. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-100)
While a trader is creating a template, a valid Save and continue on the commodity page goes to the notification overview. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-100)
notes: Unchanged from the existing row: no requirement behind it moved. Combines the change-context return (req-119) with the template-creation return (req-091): both are where the commodity pages go back to, on the same two controllers. c-021 (ruled): Commodity details returns to check answers too, carried by ?change=1. Depends on inc-015 in this area, and on the templates area's rows that let a trader create a template and edit it from its review (inc-156, inc-159): the real service has no notification templates today, so the template criteria cannot be observed until those land.

increments.title: Main import reason page edits a template from its review
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader edit a template page by page from the template's review. Opened that way, the main import reason page's Back link goes to the template's review, and saving saves the template and returns there with a confirmation.
acceptanceCriteria: Opened from a template's review, the main import reason page's Back link goes to that template's review (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-009)

Opened from a template's review, a valid 'Save and continue' saves the reason to the template and returns to the template's review, showing '<title> has been updated' with the template's title (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-009)
The template's review then shows the reason just saved, and the notification the template came from is unchanged (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-009)
notes: Unchanged from the existing row. Kept apart because it needs the templates area's rows that let a template be reviewed and changed (inc-156, inc-159), or the combiner merges it into the templates row that brings editing to each journey page if that row covers every page. No template mode exists in the real frontend today.

increments.title: Arrival details while creating or editing a template
increments.detail: A template is reused across consignments, so a one-off arrival date does not belong in it: while a template is being created, arrival details does not ask for the arrival date and the section is complete without one. A trader editing a template from its review is sent back to the template review.
acceptanceCriteria: While a template is being created, arrival details shows no arrival date question, and the other four questions are shown as usual (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-022; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p11-007)

While a template is being created, saving arrival details saves no arrival date, and the template's arrival details count as complete without one (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-023, prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-056)

When arrival details is opened to edit a template from its review, the Back link goes to the template review (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-006; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p11-006)

When arrival details is opened to edit a template from its review, Save and continue saves and returns to the template review (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-053, prototype-dr2-1-source-p6-083)
notes: Combines req-290 (no arrival date in a template) and req-291 (return to template review): both are arrival details' behaviour in template mode. The frontend has no templates today, so this row keeps its dependencies on the templates rows that create a template through the journey and add the template review page (inc-156, inc-159), and on inc-028 for the save routing. Kept in the type-question-and-templates theme so the other arrival rows are not held up by templates.
Criterion 2 no longer lists which other answers make the section complete: that rule is req-331 (exists) less the arrival date, so the criterion states only the change.

increments.title: Template creation leaves out Upload documents
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 keeps documents out of templates, because a document belongs to one consignment, and Sam's 9 October ruling confirms a template never offers documents. While a trader is creating a template, Upload documents is not a step of the journey and the template's overview offers no Documents task. The same ruling says the prototype's guards on the page's own address are not required, so none is built. No real service has templates yet, so this lands once the templates area has built template creation.
acceptanceCriteria: While creating a template, Save and continue on the transporter step goes to the page for Consignment addresses (roles and addresses), passing over Upload documents. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1517-1525; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 21)

While creating a template, the template's overview shows no 'Upload documents' task and no Documents section to follow. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:1519-1521; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 21)
notes: Kept apart: it can only be observed once template creation exists, which the templates area builds. The combiner must make this row depend on the templates area's row that lets a trader create a template and walk its journey (inc-155 today); that is a real ordering need, not a layer split. Where template mode lives in the shared flow is for the templates area's rows to set.

Re-distil after Sam's 9 October ruling (claim 21; conflict c-238): the two criteria for redirecting the page's address in template mode are gone, replaced by the overview having no Documents task. No longer depends on the page-address row, which is out of scope; depends on the journey-foundation step-order row instead, because the first criterion rests on Consignment addresses following Upload documents.

increments.title: The transporter list's buttons when amending a notification or editing a template
increments.detail: When the transporter list is reached while amending a submitted notification, or while editing a template from its review, it ends with the controls DR2.1 gives those modes, so the trader can return to where they came from.
acceptanceCriteria: When the notification is being amended, the transporter list ends with a primary 'Save and return' that goes back to the review, a secondary 'Save and continue' and a link-style 'Save and return to overview'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html isAmend branch; prototype-dr2-1-source-p7-043)

When the transporter list is edited from a template review, it ends with a single 'Save and return' button, which goes back to the template, and a 'Cancel' link back to the template. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html isTemplateReview branch; app/routes.js:3335; prototype-dr2-1-source-p7-044)
notes: Combines the two alternative-mode control sets (req-407, req-408): both change only the list's closing controls. Needs amending a notification (inc-004) and editing a template from its review (inc-159) to exist first; the combiner may fold these criteria into those rows if they change the shared save controls for every page at once.

increments.title: Back links follow the context a page was opened in
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 builds every journey page's Back link from how the page was reached: to the overview from an overview task, to the template's review page from a template review, and otherwise to the previous page in the step order, including when the page was opened from the review page's Change link. The context comes from the service's own journey state (the opening run, ?change=1, template editing), not from a from=hub or from=review marker. Today task pages point Back at the overview whatever context they were opened in.
acceptanceCriteria: A page opened from its overview task has a 'Back' link to the overview. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498)

A page reached by 'Save and continue' in the opening run has a 'Back' link to the previous page in the step order: 'Main reason for import' goes back to 'What are you importing?', and 'Commodity details' goes back to 'Main reason for import'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498, app/routes.js:1495-1501)

A page opened from a Change link on the review page has a 'Back' link to the previous page in the step order, not to the review page; 'Save and continue' there still returns to the review page. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 21)
A page opened from a template's review page has a 'Back' link to that template's review page. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:488-498)
Pages behind 'Roles and addresses' (the party pickers and the CPH number page) keep their 'Back' link to 'Roles and addresses'. (repo:tests tests/animals/e2e/features/cph-scope.spec.ts:66-73)

sources.ref: claims 21 and 39 (?change=1 stays; no from=hub marker)

notes: One slice (req-1616, c-206, c-276). Depends on the opening-run step-order row (the previous page is taken from the new order) and on the templates area's row that lets a template be edited from its review page (req-1358): the template-review criterion cannot be observed before that context exists, and a requirement cannot be split across rows.
Re-distil: the detail now says the context is the service's own state, not a URL marker (c-276, 9 October ruling), and the 'Roles and addresses' Back link, previously only in notes, is a criterion.

increments.title: Germinal products notifications on their own list and cards
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 lists germinal products notifications only on the germinal products list, counts them in packages and names the commodity by species and product type. The 2026-10-09 ruling builds the germinal cards (p1-050), so this no longer waits on a decision; it waits only for germinal products notifications to exist and reach the INS read model with their category, species, product type and package count, which the germinal products set and the notification record build.

increments.title: The stub's countries and ports match real MDM, and every captured country and port fixture is recaptured from it
increments.detail: Sam's 9 October ruling accepts a stub tidy-up so the stub matches real MDM wherever the real thing exists, ahead of the reference list rows. Today the stub's ports are 78 hand-kept Great Britain ports carrying only an id, a code and a name, and its countries are a hand-kept list that ignores the blocks filter. After this change the stub serves MDM's real port and country records, whole and in MDM's order, filters countries by block as MDM does, and the animals frontend's, the INS frontend's and the tests repo's captured country and port data are recaptured from it, so every later list row is built and tested against what MDM really serves. MDM's duplicate and misspelt ports stay: they are MDM's content, reported to the MDM team, and no test pins them.
acceptanceCriteria: Locally and in CDP dev, the stub's MDM ports call answers with MDM's real port records in MDM's order, in place of the 78 hand-kept ports, each record carrying its traffic (Airport, Port or Rail), its address and its status (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-004, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-150, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-151; repo:stub repo-stub-p2-056, repo-stub-p2-057, repo-stub-p2-081)

Locally and in CDP dev, the stub serves each port record whole, including fields its own models do not name, so each port's traffic is in the response reference data reads (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-154)

Locally and in CDP dev, the ports the stub serves keep MDM's duplicate and misspelt entries and GB MID's non-breaking spaces as MDM has them, and no value MDM masks is filled in (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-151, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-153, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-163)

Locally and in CDP dev, the stub's ports call still answers as MDM does: 200 OK with the port list in its result field, needing a subscription key header whose value it does not check (repo:stub repo-stub-p2-058, repo-stub-p2-060, repo-stub-p2-061)

Locally, the port of entry search on arrival details offers the tidied stub's ports, as reference data serves them, rather than the 78 hand-kept ones (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-150; repo:referencedata repo-referencedata-p1-037)

In the animals frontend's stub mode, the port of entry search offers the same ports, in the same order, as reference data serves from the tidied stub, and no port check is marked as waiting on an endpoint that is not built (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-157, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-158)

Locally and in CDP dev, the stub's MDM countries call without a blocks filter answers all 250 countries in MDM's order with their full real records, in place of today's hand-kept list, and no value MDM masks is filled in (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-147, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-150, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-152, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-153; repo:stub repo-stub-p2-011, repo-stub-p2-012)

Locally and in CDP dev, the stub's countries call for the GBNAG_SPS_EX block answers the 32 countries in that block, as MDM does (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-155; repo:stub repo-stub-p2-005, repo-stub-p2-043, repo-stub-p2-079)

Locally and in CDP dev, the stub serves each country record whole, including fields its own models do not name (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-154; repo:stub repo-stub-p2-008, repo-stub-p2-046)

The stub's own tests check the regenerated countries and ports fixtures, and check that the blocks filter answers 32 countries for GBNAG_SPS_EX and 250 without it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-156; repo:stub repo-stub-p2-069, repo-stub-p2-070)

In the animals frontend's stub mode, the country lists offer the same countries, names and order as reference data serves from the tidied stub, and no country check is marked as waiting on an endpoint that is not built (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-157, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-158; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p4-077; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p5-016)

In the INS frontend's stub mode, the address book's Country select offers the countries captured from the reference data service's unfiltered list, not the four hand-typed ones (United Kingdom, France, Germany, Ireland) (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-143, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-144, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-159; repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p3-028)

The end-to-end specs take their country names from the recaptured countries fixture, the tests repo keeps no unused hand-kept list of country rows, and every spec that counts the unfiltered country list expects the count served, 249 places on the local stack rather than 31 (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-160, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-161, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-162)

increments.title: A germinal products notification starts in its own set, with its own draft, category and origin page

This row lays that set down and proves it with its first page: a trader who chooses Germinal products on the type question, or Create new on the INS germinal products list, gets a new Draft notification with a GBN-AG reference, stored with the category germinal products, and lands on the germinal set's own copy of the origin page. Each set opens only its own category's notifications, the set's root hands on to the INS germinal products list, and every germinal page carries the shared service chrome pointed at the germinal set. The germinal set's checks run inside the existing animals Playwright project.
acceptanceCriteria: Choosing 'Germinal products' on 'What are you importing?', or 'Create new' on the INS germinal products list, creates a new notification with status Draft and a reference of the form GBN-AG-<two-digit year>-<six characters>, shown in the status strip, and lands on the germinal products set's 'Origin of the import' page. increments.title: Germinal Commodity details checks weight and packages, listing errors by question

Depends on the germinal set's foundation row (germinal-products area: 'A germinal products notification starts in its own set, with its own draft, category and origin page'), which the combiner should add to dependsOn, and on every live transporter row it copies (inc-037 to inc-041), so the copy is taken after the live twin is built.
